evidence.claim: Turn entry is GeminiClient.sendMessageStream which invokes processTurn via yield* so inner events pass through.
evidence.notes: processTurn returns Turn but yields ServerGeminiStreamEvent; yield* merges them.

evidence.claim: Turn.run yields events in a deterministic per-chunk order: Retry? -> AgentExecution*? -> (Thought*, Content?, ToolCallRequest*, Citation?, Finished?), plus UserCancelled/InvalidStream/Error terminal fallbacks.
evidence.notes: Finished is gated on finishReason presence; Citation is only emitted when at least one citation exists and finishReason is present.

evidence.claim: Two continuation loops exist (invalid-stream retry + next-speaker continuation) and both are bounded by MAX_TURNS = 100.
evidence.notes: Math.min(turns, MAX_TURNS) caps even user-supplied turns argument.

evidence.claim: Loop detection runs twice per turn (turnStarted before turn.run; addAndCheck on every yielded event). Recovery uses a synthetic system-text message injection via recursive sendMessageStream.
evidence.notes: Establishes an existing synthetic-injection precedent that is simpler than synthetic-tool registration (see contradiction C-02.6).

evidence.claim: Model routing is consumed inside processTurn after loop detection; result is sticky per prompt_id via currentSequenceModel.
evidence.notes: Three reset triggers: prompt_id change, CoreEvent.ModelChanged, clearCurrentSequenceModel().

evidence.claim: Token usage is captured at two layers: per-chunk in GeminiChat.processStreamResponse (via chatRecordingService.recordMessageTokens and lastPromptTokenCount), and per-LLM-call in LoggingContentGenerator telemetry events tagged by LlmRole.
evidence.notes: Pollux SPEC §8 TurnLog duplicates this capture; see contradiction C-02.2.

evidence.claim: ContentGenerator chain is a decorator stack: concrete generator (GoogleGenAI.models | CodeAssistServer | FakeContentGenerator) always wrapped by LoggingContentGenerator, optionally wrapped outermost by RecordingContentGenerator.
evidence.notes: Recording wrap is at contentGenerator.ts:298-300 gated on config.recordResponses.

evidence.claim: Retries exist at three distinct layers: connection-phase retryWithBackoff in client.generateContent; mid-stream streamWithRetries in geminiChat (MID_STREAM_RETRY_OPTIONS.maxAttempts = 4); InvalidStream continuation in client.processTurn (one-shot 'System: Please continue.').
evidence.notes: Mid-stream retry distinguishes connection-phase vs iteration-phase errors; only iteration-phase non-400 errors retry mid-stream.

evidence.claim: LlmRole tagging is carried end-to-end from Turn.run -> GeminiChat.sendMessageStream -> ContentGenerator.generateContent into telemetry events. The enum already includes MAIN, SUBAGENT, and 9 UTILITY_* roles including UTILITY_ROUTER and UTILITY_LOOP_DETECTOR.
evidence.notes: Pollux advisor slot: add UTILITY_ADVISOR to LlmRole; telemetry attribution then flows automatically.

evidence.claim: Hooks fire at four sites across the core turn. BeforeAgent and AfterAgent wrap the whole prompt outer loop in client.sendMessageStream. BeforeModel (implicit) and AfterModel fire per-chunk inside geminiChat.processStreamResponse. AfterModel may throw AgentExecutionStoppedError (terminal) or AgentExecutionBlockedError (non-terminal with optional syntheticResponse).
evidence.notes: agent_execution_stopped causes Turn.run to return (terminal); agent_execution_blocked causes it to continue consuming.

evidence.claim: Compression has three outcomes (COMPRESSED, CONTENT_TRUNCATED, failure). Only COMPRESSED yields a ChatCompressed event from processTurn; CONTENT_TRUNCATED mutates history in place without emitting an event.
evidence.notes: COMPRESSED rebuilds the chat via startChat(newHistory, resumedData) and preserves the conversation recording file path.

evidence.claim: No advisor_consultation synthetic tool or Pollux runtime integration exists in the fork. The packages/core/src/pollux namespace contains only a 171-byte index.ts and an empty benchmark/ directory.
sessionTurnCount is session-scoped (per GeminiClient instance), not prompt-scoped; it survives across sendMessageStream invocations and drives MaxSessionTurns via config.getMaxSessionTurns().
evidence.notes: Distinct from MAX_TURNS (hard cap on continuation recursion).

contradictions.description: C-02.1 Stream pause/resume is not a turn-level primitive. Turn.run is an async generator; 'pausing' must happen at the caller seam, not inside Turn.run.
C-02.2 Pollux logger proposal duplicates existing token capture in LoggingContentGenerator and ChatRecordingService.recordMessageTokens. A new logger would duplicate or diverge.

C-02.3 'Single-model baseline' premise in spec is false. The core already invokes at least 7 distinct LlmRole utility models per normal turn (router, loop detector, next speaker, summarizer, compressor, edit corrector, autocomplete, fast-ack). Benchmark A/E conditions must hold these constant.

C-02.4 'Don't touch GeminiChat directly' advice in spec is too absolute. Loop detection is not inside GeminiChat; compression is a service (ChatCompressionService). The actual constraint is: don't mutate GeminiChat.history from outside the class.

C-02.5 Spec advisor client uses contentGenerator.generateContent directly, but the appropriate utility for JSON-shape output is BaseLlmClient.generateJson which already handles parsing, retries, and validation.

C-02.6 Synthetic-tool injection is declared 'most natural', but existing synthetic-message injection precedents (_recoverFromLoop and next-speaker continuation) use plain recursive sendMessageStream with text and are simpler.
C-02.7 Heuristic 'turn count > 8' in spec fires long before session-level MaxSessionTurns and MAX_TURNS=100. Should be framed as an earlier advisory signal, not a cap.

C-02.8 Spec's phrase 'wire interceptor into client.ts at processTurn()' underspecifies whether the hook runs per-event or per-turn. The correct seam is between turn.run emission and the yield event at client.ts:773.

risks.description: R-02.1 Event-ordering regressions on any edit to processTurn's for-await loop (17 yield sites, interleaved with loop detection and telemetry).
risks.suggestedGuard: Deterministic event-transcript snapshot test over a scripted mock stream covering retry + function call + loop-detected + finish.

risks.description: R-02.2 currentSequenceModel stickiness inversion: three reset triggers (prompt_id change, CoreEvent.ModelChanged, clearCurrentSequenceModel). No test asserts all three.
risks.suggestedGuard: Test asserting ModelInfo fires exactly once per prompt_id and CoreEvent.ModelChanged between prompts does not suppress it.

risks.description: R-02.3 updateTelemetryTokenCount runs after every yielded event including Error/LoopDetected. On error paths, lastPromptTokenCount may be stale relative to the event, producing mis-attributed telemetry.
risks.suggestedGuard: Unit test where stream throws mid-chunk and assert setLastPromptTokenCount is called with pre-throw value.

risks.description: R-02.4 IDE context injection pushes a synthetic user message to history. Early return after injection (e.g., ContextWindowWillOverflow) leaves the injection in place for the next turn.
risks.suggestedGuard: Test for ContextWindowWillOverflow immediately after IDE-context injection; assert no double injection next turn.

risks.description: R-02.5 AgentExecutionStoppedError path does not yield a syntheticResponse chunk even if the hook provides one; AgentExecutionBlockedError does. Asymmetry is undocumented.
risks.suggestedGuard: Test exercising AgentExecutionStoppedError with syntheticResponse; codify the design.

risks.description: R-02.6 Compression COMPRESSED path rebuilds GeminiChat via startChat(newHistory, resumedData); any in-flight telemetry span referencing the old chat is orphaned.
risks.suggestedGuard: Cross-compartment: compartment 11 should confirm span scoping.

OQ-02.2 Can checkNextSpeaker stall or be rate-limited, blocking turn completion synchronously?
OQ-02.3 Continuation recursion passes the original signal (client.ts:836), not the linked one. Is there a dangling abort chain on multi-turn continuations?
